newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel traffic blocked three hours by strike.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel traffic blocked three hours by strike.

text.p: French strikers blocked tourist and truck traffic through the Channel Tunnel linking France and Britain for three hours on Wednesday in a protest at working conditions.
Drivers sat in their vehicles in stifling sunshine as the stoppage, the first major action by Eurotunnel unions, created tailbacks several km (miles) long at the French terminal.
Most of those trapped were British and Dutch tourists. Some of them argued bitterly with the strikers, accusing them of taking passengers hostage.

No Shuttle rail services left Coquelles during the strike and only one train carrying trucks departed. At the British end of the Channel Tunnel at Folkestone, Shuttle services were running late and dwindled to just one departure every hour.
French strikers lifted pickets at toll booths at around 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) after winning a management promise of talks later in the day to review working conditions.
Officials estimated that only about 100 workers heeded the strike call. Eurotunnel employs just over 3,000 staff, including 1,600 French workers.
Freight traffic and Eurostar passenger trains, run by the state railways SNCF, were not hit by the action.

The unions want better working conditions and accuse management of ignoring grievances over salaries and working hours. They have proposed meeting management representatives, who have suggested July 29 for a first round of talks.
One of the workers' 22 demands is for overtime pay to start immediately after the end of a shift. Currently, workers have to stay on at least 30 minutes extra to qualify for overtime.
"We want a timetable for the talks. If we don't get it, the movement will harden," said Franck Heranwal, of the Communist-led CGT union.
